haiku-low.q1: After the message and its outbox row commit, with seq assigned. The ack means the message is saved.
haiku-low.q2: The sender gets an error. No outbox row exists, so nobody receives it. The retry must carry the same msg_id, so no second copy is created.
haiku-low.q3: When its presence entry expires, 30 seconds after the last heartbeat. Heartbeats are sent every 10 seconds.
haiku-low.q4: The recipient is treated as offline for that message. The worker writes an Offline Inbox entry and sends a push. A late ack means one duplicate copy is dropped.
haiku-low.q5: The failure is logged and not retried. The inbox entry already exists, so the message still arrives on reconnect.
haiku-low.q6: Ordered by conversation, then by seq. Clients drop repeats by message id, and keep seen msg_ids to do so.
haiku-low.q7: The outbox row is written in the same transaction as the message, so it survives a crash. The Outbox Relay publishes unpublished rows after restart.
haiku-low.q8: In the Presence Registry, one entry per user holding its Gateway node. The entry's 30-second TTL expires it when heartbeats stop.
haiku-low.q9: The Fan-out Worker sends it through the recipient's Gateway to the open connection. It waits up to 5 seconds for the client's ack, which means it reached the device.
haiku-low.q10: In the Offline Inbox, one entry per user and message. Written when a recipient is offline or unacked within 5 seconds. Removed by client ack, or after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: The user's Offline Inbox entries, then the message bodies from Message Store, ordered by conversation and seq.
haiku-low.q12: The event's offset is not committed, so the whole event is redelivered. Recipients drop duplicates, and inbox writes are keyed so repeats are harmless.

sonnet.q1: Only after the message and its outbox row are committed in the Message Store transaction. The ack (msg_id + seq) means the message is saved.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error. No outbox row exists, so nothing is fanned out and no recipient gets anything. The retry must carry the same msg_id.
sonnet.q3: When the presence entry expires, 30 seconds after the last heartbeat (heartbeats are every 10 s). A user is online only while the entry exists.
sonnet.q4: The recipient is treated as offline for that message. The worker writes an Offline Inbox entry and sends a push. If the ack arrives late, the client holds the message twice and drops one copy.
sonnet.q5: The failure is logged and not retried. The inbox entry already exists, so the message still arrives on reconnect.
sonnet.q6: Ordered by conversation, then by seq. Duplicates are dropped by the client using msg_id (it tracks msg_ids already seen).
sonnet.q7: The outbox row was written in the same transaction as the message, so it survives the crash. The Outbox Relay publishes unpublished rows, so fan-out still runs. The sender's retry gets the same ack.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Registry, one entry per user holding the Gateway node. The entry has a TTL of 30 s and is deleted automatically when no heartbeat refreshes it.
sonnet.q9: The Fan-out Worker reads the Presence Registry to find the recipient's Gateway node, sends the message through that Gateway, which pushes it to the client's WebSocket. The client's ack (waited up to 5 s) confirms arrival.
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox, one entry per (user, message) holding conversation_id, seq and msg_id (references only). It is written by the Fan-out Worker when the recipient is offline or does not ack within 5 s. An entry is removed by the client's ack on reconnect, or expires after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: The user's Offline Inbox entries are read, and the message bodies are read from the Message Store.
sonnet.q12: The offset is not committed, so the whole event is delivered again. Recipients who already got it receive it again and drop the duplicate. Inbox writes are keyed by (user, msg_id), so repeats are harmless.
